title: SLO Conversation Quickcards for Platform Engineers (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, noisy sketch for seller/SE -> platform engineer quickcards focused on SLO conversations. The goal: give sellers and SEs 4–6 short, engineer-friendly talking points and a one-slide fallback matrix to move from qual to technical next steps fast. Not polished — notes to self + sample lines + suggested checks for pilots.

Audience:
- Platform engineers, SREs, infra architects at mid-market/enterprise accounts
- Primary persona: cares about availability, predictable tail latency, capacity isolation, auditability

Format (how to use):
- 30s: opener (what we need to know)
- 60s: value proposition in platform terms
- 90s: canary/rollback + fallback plan (explicit)
- Checklist: immediate technical asks for pilot scoping

Quickcard A — Opening (30s)
- Seller: "We help you keep model-powered features within a predictable latency and cost envelope while giving you clear fallbacks if GPU capacity is constrained."
- Why it matters to you: "No surprises in P95/P99 latency; we map model variants to capacity tiers so your user-facing SLAs stay met even during spikes."
- Signal to probe: "How are you currently measuring tail latency and what SLOs do you have for third-party model calls?"

Quickcard B — Platform value in engineer language (60s)
- One-liner: "Redwood provides a runtime + routing layer so you can pin models, route by policy (latency/cost/region), and fail gracefully to compatible variants."
- Key capabilities to call out: autoscaling for Dedicated pools; transparent per-token latency/cost breakdowns; prefix/KV caching for repeated flows.
- Evidence snippet: "We run canaries with traffic shadowing and have dashboard traces per-request so your team can correlate code deployments to latency spikes."

Quickcard C — Canary/Canary-fallback script (90s)
- Plain script: "Start canary: 5% traffic -> dedicated pool, 5% -> hosted (control). Run 3x 10-min bursts with real traffic mix. Monitor P95/P99 and model quality on 100 golden prompts. If latency regresses >20% or error rate >1% -> rollback and route to fallback model variant (quantized / smaller)."
- Suggested fallback order (simple): 1) same model smaller batch size on Dedicated, 2) compatible quantized variant (compatible output shape), 3) smaller model in hosted with result enrichment (cache + post-filter).
- Probe: "Do you have canary traffic we can mirror? If not, can we start with replay of representative logs?"

Quickcard D — Risk & objection handling (engineer style)
- "We don't want blackbox network dependencies": Point to audit logs + VPC private deployment option; list KMS integrations.
- "Fallback model will change outputs": We recommend a deterministic validation set (50–200 prompts) and automated diff checks + rollback on quality drift.
- "Cost unpredictability": Show per-token breakdown and reserved capacity commit options with burst capacity controls.

Checklist for Pilot Scoping (immediate asks)
- SLA targets: desired P95/P99 (ms) and acceptable error rate
- Traffic profile: qps, typical sequence length, peak burst multiplier
- Privacy/security: does data need to be VPC/on-prem? Any compliance constraints?
- Model expectations: preferred family, allowed quantization/variants
- Observability hooks: sample request/response trace ids, golden prompt set (CSV)

One-slide fallback matrix (sketch) — how to present
- Rows: "Problem observed" (latency surge / capacity saturation / model drift / error spike)
- Columns: "Immediate action (0–15m)", "Short term (15–120m)", "Postmortem/Next steps"
- Example cell (latency surge): Immediate: route low-latency tier, throttle non-critical traffic; Short term: scale Dedicated pool, enable prefix cache; Postmortem: tune batching policy, consider reserved capacity.

Evidence & small experiments to propose in pilot
- 1) Short Traffic Mirror (48h): mirror 5% of production to canary pool + latency comparison dashboard
- 2) Golden prompt quality diff (every 30m) — automated alerts on >2% regression in top-1 match
- 3) Throughput test with synthetic burst (10x baseline for 5m) to validate autoscale/burst behavior

Notes to SEs (quick reminders)
- Bring a concrete golden prompt set — nothing too large, 50–200 items is sufficient for early signal
- Ask for a simple Grafana endpoint or sample traces — we can instrument if they can't share dashboards
- Keep fallback decision explicit in the contract: which model variant is acceptable as "fallback"?

Open questions / TODOs
- Get metrics from infra team on typical sequence length distribution (critical for kernel selection implications) — action: Arjun to ping infra@account
- Build 1-pager showing "fallback delta" (latency/cost/quality) for our top 3 model families — Maya to draft
- Confirm SSO/KMS flow for VPC private deployments with security — Jordan to start discovery call with security ops

References / ready snippets to paste into a buyer email
- "We recommend a 2-week pilot: mirror traffic, run golden prompt validation and a synthetic burst test. If you hit latency regressions, we fall back to a smaller quantized model and use cached prefixes to protect hot paths."

Slack seed links (internal)
- #go-to-market-pilot-templates, #platform-seller-snippets, #infra-canary-runbook

Revision history (short)
- 2025-11-10 initial sketch (Leah)
- 2025-12-04 added fallback matrix example (Arjun)
- 2026-02-15 added pilot experiment checklist + TODOs (Maya)

-- end of sketch --

(Notes: intended to be split into 2–3 slides + 1 battlecard cheat-sheet. Keep language short and less "salesy"; aim for engineer credibility.)
